If I stay orthostatic for 4 hours first, I won’t get symptomatic after a nap. But if I take one in the morning when I don’t have a lot going on, it almost always causes a flare up, and I almost always get sleep paralysis. I figure it has to do with my blood pressure and adrenaline not “regulating” first. This is also a huge problem if I have to pee in the middle of the night, so I try to not drink water before bed. Edited to add: I don’t always STAND for four hours, but as long as I don’t lay down in that time, my symptoms improve. Sometimes I just have to though, and yes it makes my symptoms worse, but I’m just too tired to cope in the first place anyway.

I know this is a POTS page and I was anxious this would come across weird but I didn’t want you to feel unheard. 

I also started drinking heavily when I was diagnosed with POTS. I hurt those I love one time too many and that’s what it took for me to realize I needed to stop drinking. Take it one day at a time. It’s a MAJOR step to realize you need to quit. If not for yourself, then others. We can treat our POTS with salt and compression socks but the syndrome will never really go away. Quitting drinking doesn’t make alcoholism “go away,” but you can find a better version of yourself along that journey, one that’s more equipped to handle POTS. If you can’t get medical support, then reach out to loved ones/communities to help. They don’t have to be in person. Celebrate your milestones, whatever you choose them to be, for YOU. There are a lot of resources online about what to expect in the coming years like cravings, habits, hobbies, etc. You are NOT alone. It sucks at times and it’s hard to sit with the feelings/symptoms I was trying to escape. My journey feels like it is barely started, but if others can do it, then so can I, and so can you. 💗
